question.prompt: Should the pair budget rise from 3 to 4 so the design can include a dedicated author-name search scenario for `Branwen Oduya`?

options.label: Keep 3-pair budget
options.detail: Proceed without a dedicated author-match scenario and leave that documented search dimension uncovered in this run.

options.label: Raise to 4 pairs
options.detail: Add the author-name matching scenario and its one test in a follow-up rework.

content.risk_rationale: Author-name matching is explicitly promised by the source, but under the 3-pair ceiling it added less risk reduction than the kept exact-title, genre-membership, and no-results paths.

content.title: Search a known title in exact and case-varied form and reach the same single-result page
content.intent: Prove that a known title search from the header routes to a shareable `/search` page, shows the headed results page, returns the documented single result for `The Iron Court`, preserves that result across lower-case and upper-case variants of the same term, and renders the documented tile fields.
content.technique_notes: Equivalence partitioning across the documented known-title search term with exact-case, lower-case, and upper-case representatives. Risk-judged interaction strength was 2 because only user-reach and change-frequency apply, but no covering array was needed because this path varies only one input family: the entered search term variant.

content.title: Search by genre name from the header and receive books from that genre
content.intent: Prove that searching `Mystery` matches on genre and returns books that belong to the `Mystery` genre while still using the standard search results presentation.
content.technique_notes: Equivalence partitioning over the documented genre-match representative `Mystery`. The search/list result-set profile applied because this path asserts membership semantics across a returned collection. Risk-judged interaction strength was 2 because only user-reach and change-frequency apply, and no covering array was needed because only the search-term class varies in this path.

content.title: Search with an unmatched term or with no term and see the explicit no-results message
content.intent: Prove that both an unmatched search term and a blank submission resolve to the same explicit `No books match your search` message instead of an empty or broken results page.
content.technique_notes: Negative/error coverage plus equivalence partitioning for two source-defined no-results representatives: an unmatched non-empty term and a blank submission. Boundary value analysis applied to the blank submission as the source-stated minimum-content input. Risk-judged interaction strength was 2 because only user-reach applies, and no covering array was needed because the path varies a single input family whose representatives are documented to share one outcome.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Ranked highest because it covers the source's most specific example and the most ACs in one path: routing, URL propagation, results heading, exact single-result behavior, case-insensitive matching, and reusable tile presentation.
[value_score] Ranked second because genre matching exercises the broader collection-membership promise rather than a single known record, making it the stronger remaining non-title search dimension.
[value_score] Ranked third because the source explicitly promises graceful no-results handling for both unmatched and blank input, and the blank case is the only source-stated input boundary.
[value_score] Ranked fourth and evicted only by budget because it adds the remaining author-match dimension but overlaps with the kept title and genre scenarios more than the kept negative path does.
[applicability] Did not apply because the search behavior in scope is results routing and matching, not field-level validation rules or submit blocking copy.
[applicability] Applied to the genre and no-results paths because the use-case promises result-set membership and empty-state behavior on a search results collection.
[applicability] Not minted as its own scenario because the source does not state accessibility-specific search promises; any applicable invariant a11y checks would need separate evidence.
[applicability] Not minted because the source states case-insensitive matching but gives no locale-specific casing or collation promise.
